html:
In the app

A level project opens with guided mode on this chapter: the panel lists the tags the program needs (Make them), shows every rung below under its fold, checks that MainRoutine verifies, and ticks these results while you run the level:

  • A socket is connected to Cam1 at 192.168.1.18:3000
  • Cam1 gets a TRIG while Inspect_Req is on
  • The answer is read back (ReadSocket brings it into Read_Resp)
  • Result_Pass and Result_Score match the answer when Insp_Done comes on
  • All 10 requests answered

Hard · par 21 s

The job

Level 20's exchange, and now the answer is used. The socket data types are in the project already. For each of the 10 requests, write TRIG, read the answer and turn it into results: Result_Pass (1 for PASS, 0 for FAIL) and Result_Score (the number after the comma, 0 to 100); then set Insp_Done. The line takes the results when Insp_Done comes on and drops Inspect_Req; clear Insp_Done when it does. The answer arrives as bytes in ReadResponse.Buf: copy them into a STRING's DATA and the count into its LEN, FIND the comma, MID out the verdict and the score (one, two or three digits) and STOD the score. +100 for each request whose results match the answer; −50 for each result tag that does not, and for Insp_Done before the answer was read; −25 for Insp_Done still on 2 s after the request drops; −50 for a request not done within 8 s.

The program

Level 20’s sequence, with the answer used: after the read, the bytes are copied into a STRING’s DATA and the count into its LEN, FIND finds the comma, MID takes the verdict and the score, STOD turns the score into a number, the result tags are set and Insp_Done raised, and it is cleared when the request drops.

Tags this lesson needs

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

TagTypeKindDescription
StepDINTbase tagThe exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry
DelAll_MsgMESSAGEbase tagSocket DeleteAllSockets (51), instance 0: clears sockets a previous run left open
Create_MsgMESSAGEbase tagSocket Create (4B), instance 0: source Create_Req (12 bytes), destination Sock_Inst
Sock_InstDINTbase tagThe socket's instance, from Socket Create
Open_MsgMESSAGEbase tagSocket OpenConnection (4C): source Open_Req, 8 bytes plus the address's 22 characters
Write_MsgMESSAGEbase tagSocket WriteSocket (4E): source Write_Req, 80 bytes (the header and the whole Buf; BufLen says how many are sent)
Read_MsgMESSAGEbase tagSocket ReadSocket (4D): source Read_Req (8 bytes), destination Read_Resp
Inspect_ReqBOOLbase tagThe line asks for an inspection: write TRIG to Cam1 and read the answer. The level sets it and clears it
Trig_CmdSTRINGbase tagThe command Cam1 inspects on
Write_ReqWriteSocketbase tagWriteSocket's request: Timeout 5000 ms, BufLen and Buf from Trig_Cmd
Read_RespReadResponsebase tagReadSocket's answer: BufLen bytes in Buf
ReplySTRINGbase tagThe answer as a string
CommaSTRINGbase tagThe separator
Comma_PosDINTbase tagWhere the comma is (1 is the first character; 0 none)
Verdict_LenDINTbase tagHow many characters the verdict has
VerdictSTRINGbase tagThe answer up to the comma
Score_AtDINTbase tagWhere the score starts
Score_LenDINTbase tagHow many characters the score has
Score_StrSTRINGbase tagThe answer after the comma
Result_ScoreDINTbase tagThe answer's score, 0 to 100
Pass_StrSTRINGbase tagThe verdict that passes
Result_PassBOOLbase tagThe answer's verdict: 1 for PASS, 0 for FAIL
Insp_DoneBOOLbase tagSet it when the result tags hold this inspection's answer; clear it when Inspect_Req drops
Retry_TTIMERbase tagTwo seconds before trying again after an error

The rungs

Watch for

The score after the comma can be one, two or three digits. Take its length from the string’s LEN, not a fixed count.

Run it

Load the program, go to Run mode and leave the level to finish (press Start on its console where it has one). The score card shows how it went, and the guided checks above tick as each result happens. A run of this program on v2.02 completed in about 15 s against a par of 21 s, with 1200 points and nothing wrong.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: FIRST SCAN: start by deleting any sockets a previous run left open. A socket stays open in the socket object until it is deleted, and there are 32 of them

pred.q: S:FS is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written.

rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung puts 5 into Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. MOV(5,Step) Move does: puts 5 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: DeleteAllSockets: CIP Generic, service 51, class 342, instance 0, path THIS
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 5, the rung sends the message DelAll_Msg (Socket DeleteAllSockets (51), instance 0: clears sockets a previous run left open).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,5) Equal asks: true when Step equals 5. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. MSG(DelAll_Msg) Message does: sends the message DelAll_Msg.

rungs.head: Rung 2

pred.q: DelAll_Msg.DN is on, DelAll_Msg.ER is on and Step is 6. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Step is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at EQU(Step,5).

rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 5 and either (DelAll_Msg.DN (the done bit of DelAll_Msg: Socket DeleteAllSockets (51), instance 0: clears sockets a previous run left open) is on) or (DelAll_Msg.ER (the error bit of DelAll_Msg: Socket DeleteAllSockets (51), instance 0: clears sockets a previous run left open) is on), the rung puts 10 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,5) Equal asks: true when Step equals 5. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(DelAll_Msg.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when DelAll_Msg.DN is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(DelAll_Msg.ER) Examine If Closed asks: true when DelAll_Msg.ER is on.
  3. MOV(10,Step) Move does: puts 10 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 5, to 10); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.
pats.think: a recipe card with numbered steps and one finger on it. Each rung only reads the line under the finger; when its line is done it moves the finger to the next number.
pats.watch: A rung further down that tests for the new step number sees it in this same scan. Rung order decides whether the next step starts now or next scan.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: CREATE: Socket Create (4B) to instance 0 makes a TCP socket and returns its instance into Sock_Inst
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 10, the rung sends the message Create_Msg (Socket Create (4B), instance 0: source Create_Req (12 bytes), destination Sock_Inst).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,10) Equal asks: true when Step equals 10. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. MSG(Create_Msg) Message does: sends the message Create_Msg.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: Every other message goes to that instance: MOV it into each one's .Instance

pred.q: Create_Msg.DN is on and Step is 10. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Open_Msg.Instance is written, Write_Msg.Instance is written, Read_Msg.Instance is written and Step is written.

rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 10 and Create_Msg.DN (the done bit of Create_Msg: Socket Create (4B), instance 0: source Create_Req (12 bytes), destination Sock_Inst) is on, the rung puts Sock_Inst (The socket's instance, from Socket Create) into Open_Msg.Instance (Socket OpenConnection (4C): source Open_Req, 8 bytes plus the address's 22 characters), puts Sock_Inst into Write_Msg.Instance (Socket WriteSocket (4E): source Write_Req, 80 bytes (the header and the whole Buf; BufLen says how many are sent)), puts Sock_Inst into Read_Msg.Instance (Socket ReadSocket (4D): source Read_Req (8 bytes), destination Read_Resp) and puts 20 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,10) Equal asks: true when Step equals 10. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Create_Msg.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Create_Msg.DN is on.
  3. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(Sock_Inst,Open_Msg.Instance) Move does: puts Sock_Inst into Open_Msg.Instance. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(Sock_Inst,Write_Msg.Instance) Move does: puts Sock_Inst into Write_Msg.Instance. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(Sock_Inst,Read_Msg.Instance) Move does: puts Sock_Inst into Read_Msg.Instance. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 4
    1. MOV(20,Step) Move does: puts 20 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 10, to 20); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: OPEN: OpenConnection (4C) connects to the address in Open_Req.DestAddr, 192.168.1.18?port=3000
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 20, the rung sends the message Open_Msg (Socket OpenConnection (4C): source Open_Req, 8 bytes plus the address's 22 characters).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,20) Equal asks: true when Step equals 20. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. MSG(Open_Msg) Message does: sends the message Open_Msg.

rungs.head: Rung 6

pred.q: Open_Msg.DN is off and Step is 20. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Step is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIC(Open_Msg.DN).

rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 20 and Open_Msg.DN (the done bit of Open_Msg: Socket OpenConnection (4C): source Open_Req, 8 bytes plus the address's 22 characters) is on, the rung puts 30 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,20) Equal asks: true when Step equals 20. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Open_Msg.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Open_Msg.DN is on.
  3. MOV(30,Step) Move does: puts 30 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 20, to 30); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: READY: the connection stays open; each request is one write and one read
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 30 and Inspect_Req (The line asks for an inspection: write TRIG to Cam1 and read the answer. The level sets it and clears it) is on, the rung puts 40 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,30) Equal asks: true when Step equals 30. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Inspect_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Inspect_Req is on.
  3. MOV(40,Step) Move does: puts 40 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 30, to 40); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: WRITE: the characters of Trig_Cmd into Buf, their count into BufLen, then WriteSocket (4E) sends BufLen bytes of Buf
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 40, the rung copies Trig_Cmd.LEN elements from Trig_Cmd.DATA[0] (The command Cam1 inspects on) to Write_Req.Buf[0] (WriteSocket's request: Timeout 5000 ms, BufLen and Buf from Trig_Cmd), puts Trig_Cmd.LEN (the length of Trig_Cmd: The command Cam1 inspects on) into Write_Req.BufLen (WriteSocket's request: Timeout 5000 ms, BufLen and Buf from Trig_Cmd) and sends the message Write_Msg (Socket WriteSocket (4E): source Write_Req, 80 bytes (the header and the whole Buf; BufLen says how many are sent)).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,40) Equal asks: true when Step equals 40. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. COP(Trig_Cmd.DATA[0],Write_Req.Buf[0],Trig_Cmd.LEN) Copy File does: copies Trig_Cmd.LEN elements from Trig_Cmd.DATA[0] to Write_Req.Buf[0].
    Path 2
    1. MOV(Trig_Cmd.LEN,Write_Req.BufLen) Move does: puts Trig_Cmd.LEN into Write_Req.BufLen. It writes every scan the rung is true.
  3. MSG(Write_Msg) Message does: sends the message Write_Msg.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 40 and Write_Msg.DN (the done bit of Write_Msg: Socket WriteSocket (4E): source Write_Req, 80 bytes (the header and the whole Buf; BufLen says how many are sent)) is on, the rung puts 50 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,40) Equal asks: true when Step equals 40. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Write_Msg.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Write_Msg.DN is on.
  3. MOV(50,Step) Move does: puts 50 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 40, to 50); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: READ: ReadSocket (4D) waits up to Read_Req.Timeout for the answer; it lands in Read_Resp, BufLen bytes in Buf
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 50, the rung sends the message Read_Msg (Socket ReadSocket (4D): source Read_Req (8 bytes), destination Read_Resp).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,50) Equal asks: true when Step equals 50. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. MSG(Read_Msg) Message does: sends the message Read_Msg.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 50 and Read_Msg.DN (the done bit of Read_Msg: Socket ReadSocket (4D): source Read_Req (8 bytes), destination Read_Resp) is on, the rung puts 60 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,50) Equal asks: true when Step equals 50. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Read_Msg.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Read_Msg.DN is on.
  3. MOV(60,Step) Move does: puts 60 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 50, to 60); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: PARSE: the bytes into a STRING (into DATA, then the count into LEN), e.g. PASS,98
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 60, the rung copies Read_Resp.BufLen elements from Read_Resp.Buf[0] (ReadSocket's answer: BufLen bytes in Buf) to Reply.DATA[0] (The answer as a string) and puts Read_Resp.BufLen (ReadSocket's answer: BufLen bytes in Buf) into Reply.LEN (the length of Reply: The answer as a string).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,60) Equal asks: true when Step equals 60. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. COP(Read_Resp.Buf[0],Reply.DATA[0],Read_Resp.BufLen) Copy File does: copies Read_Resp.BufLen elements from Read_Resp.Buf[0] to Reply.DATA[0].
    Path 2
    1. MOV(Read_Resp.BufLen,Reply.LEN) Move does: puts Read_Resp.BufLen into Reply.LEN. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 60, the rung finds Comma (The separator) in Reply (The answer as a string) from position 1, the place into Comma_Pos (Where the comma is (1 is the first character; 0 none)).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,60) Equal asks: true when Step equals 60. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. FIND(Reply,Comma,1,Comma_Pos) Find String does: finds Comma in Reply from position 1, the place into Comma_Pos.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: The verdict is before it, the score after it (STOD makes the digits a DINT)

pred.q: Step is 60 and Comma_Pos is 2. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Verdict_Len is written, MID runs, Score_At is written, Score_Len is written, MID runs and STOD runs.

rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 60 and Comma_Pos (Where the comma is (1 is the first character; 0 none)) is greater than 1, the rung makes Verdict_Len (How many characters the verdict has) = Comma_Pos − 1, takes Verdict_Len characters of Reply (The answer as a string) from position 1 into Verdict (The answer up to the comma), makes Score_At (Where the score starts) = Comma_Pos + 1, makes Score_Len (How many characters the score has) = Reply.LEN (the length of Reply: The answer as a string) − Comma_Pos, takes Score_Len characters of Reply from position Score_At into Score_Str (The answer after the comma) and reads the text Score_Str as a number into Result_Score (The answer's score, 0 to 100).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,60) Equal asks: true when Step equals 60. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. GRT(Comma_Pos,1) Greater Than asks: true when Comma_Pos is greater than 1.
  3. SUB(Comma_Pos,1,Verdict_Len) Subtract does: makes Verdict_Len = Comma_Pos − 1. Every scan the rung is true.
  4. MID(Reply,Verdict_Len,1,Verdict) Middle String does: takes Verdict_Len characters of Reply from position 1 into Verdict.
  5. ADD(Comma_Pos,1,Score_At) Add does: makes Score_At = Comma_Pos + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
  6. SUB(Reply.LEN,Comma_Pos,Score_Len) Subtract does: makes Score_Len = Reply.LEN − Comma_Pos. Every scan the rung is true.
  7. MID(Reply,Score_Len,Score_At,Score_Str) Middle String does: takes Score_Len characters of Reply from position Score_At into Score_Str.
  8. STOD(Score_Str,Result_Score) String to DINT does: reads the text Score_Str as a number into Result_Score.

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 60, Comma_Pos (Where the comma is (1 is the first character; 0 none)) is greater than 1 and Verdict (The answer up to the comma) equals Pass_Str (The verdict that passes), the rung latches Result_Pass (The answer's verdict: 1 for PASS, 0 for FAIL) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,60) Equal asks: true when Step equals 60. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. GRT(Comma_Pos,1) Greater Than asks: true when Comma_Pos is greater than 1.
  3. EQU(Verdict,Pass_Str) Equal asks: true when Verdict equals Pass_Str. Both values are compared every scan.
  4. OTL(Result_Pass) Output Latch does: latches Result_Pass on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Result_Pass stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: Rung 16

pred.q: Step is 60, Comma_Pos is 1, Verdict is 11 and Pass_Str is 48. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Result_Pass is left as it was. It stops at GRT(Comma_Pos,1).

rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 60, Comma_Pos (Where the comma is (1 is the first character; 0 none)) is greater than 1 and Verdict (The answer up to the comma) is not Pass_Str (The verdict that passes), the rung unlatches Result_Pass (The answer's verdict: 1 for PASS, 0 for FAIL).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,60) Equal asks: true when Step equals 60. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. GRT(Comma_Pos,1) Greater Than asks: true when Comma_Pos is greater than 1.
  3. NEQ(Verdict,Pass_Str) Not Equal asks: true when Verdict is not Pass_Str.
  4. OTU(Result_Pass) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Result_Pass. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Result_Pass when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 17
rungs.comment: The results are in: Insp_Done tells the line
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 60 and Comma_Pos (Where the comma is (1 is the first character; 0 none)) is greater than 1, the rung latches Insp_Done (Set it when the result tags hold this inspection's answer; clear it when Inspect_Req drops) on and puts 70 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,60) Equal asks: true when Step equals 60. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. GRT(Comma_Pos,1) Greater Than asks: true when Comma_Pos is greater than 1.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Insp_Done) Output Latch does: latches Insp_Done on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(70,Step) Move does: puts 70 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 60, to 70); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.
Insp_Done stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 18
rungs.comment: No comma: not an answer this program understands; start over

pred.q: Step is 60 and Comma_Pos is 0. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written.

rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 60 and Comma_Pos (Where the comma is (1 is the first character; 0 none)) is at most 1, the rung puts 95 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,60) Equal asks: true when Step equals 60. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. LEQ(Comma_Pos,1) Less Than or Equal asks: true when Comma_Pos is at most 1.
  3. MOV(95,Step) Move does: puts 95 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 60, to 95); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 19
rungs.comment: The line has taken it and dropped the request: clear Insp_Done, ready for the next
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 70 and Inspect_Req (The line asks for an inspection: write TRIG to Cam1 and read the answer. The level sets it and clears it) is off, the rung unlatches Insp_Done (Set it when the result tags hold this inspection's answer; clear it when Inspect_Req drops) and puts 30 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,70) Equal asks: true when Step equals 70. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIO(Inspect_Req) Examine If Open asks: true when Inspect_Req is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Insp_Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Insp_Done. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(30,Step) Move does: puts 30 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 70, to 30); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 20
rungs.comment: ERRORS: a message that fails (no camera, the connection dropped, no answer in time) waits and starts over from deleting the sockets

pred.q: Create_Msg.ER is off, Open_Msg.ER is on, Write_Msg.ER is on, Read_Msg.ER is on and Step is 10. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Step is not written (it keeps its value). None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: When either (Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 10 and Create_Msg.ER (the error bit of Create_Msg: Socket Create (4B), instance 0: source Create_Req (12 bytes), destination Sock_Inst) is on), (Step equals 20 and Open_Msg.ER (the error bit of Open_Msg: Socket OpenConnection (4C): source Open_Req, 8 bytes plus the address's 22 characters) is on), (Step equals 40 and Write_Msg.ER (the error bit of Write_Msg: Socket WriteSocket (4E): source Write_Req, 80 bytes (the header and the whole Buf; BufLen says how many are sent)) is on) or (Step equals 50 and Read_Msg.ER (the error bit of Read_Msg: Socket ReadSocket (4D): source Read_Req (8 bytes), destination Read_Resp) is on), the rung puts 95 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 4 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. EQU(Step,10) Equal asks: true when Step equals 10. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. XIC(Create_Msg.ER) Examine If Closed asks: true when Create_Msg.ER is on.
    Path 2
    1. EQU(Step,20) Equal asks: true when Step equals 20. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. XIC(Open_Msg.ER) Examine If Closed asks: true when Open_Msg.ER is on.
    Path 3
    1. EQU(Step,40) Equal asks: true when Step equals 40. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. XIC(Write_Msg.ER) Examine If Closed asks: true when Write_Msg.ER is on.
    Path 4
    1. EQU(Step,50) Equal asks: true when Step equals 50. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. XIC(Read_Msg.ER) Examine If Closed asks: true when Read_Msg.ER is on.
  2. MOV(95,Step) Move does: puts 95 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 10, to 95); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 21
rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 95, the rung runs the timer Retry_T (Two seconds before trying again after an error) toward 2000 ms (2 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,95) Equal asks: true when Step equals 95. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. TON(Retry_T,2000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Retry_T toward 2000 ms (2 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Retry_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 22

pred.q: Retry_T.DN is on and Step is 95. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written.

rungs.words: When Step (The exchange's step: 5 delete all sockets, 10 create, 20 connect, 30 ready, 40 write TRIG, 50 read the answer, 60 parse, 70 wait for the request to drop, 95 wait and retry) equals 95 and Retry_T.DN (the done bit of Retry_T: Two seconds before trying again after an error) is on, the rung puts 5 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,95) Equal asks: true when Step equals 95. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Retry_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Retry_T.DN is on.
  3. MOV(5,Step) Move does: puts 5 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 95, to 5); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

DelAll_Msg.desc: Socket DeleteAllSockets (51), instance 0: clears sockets a previous run left open

Create_Msg.desc: Socket Create (4B), instance 0: source Create_Req (12 bytes), destination Sock_Inst

Sock_Inst.desc: The socket's instance, from Socket Create

Open_Msg.desc: Socket OpenConnection (4C): source Open_Req, 8 bytes plus the address's 22 characters

Write_Msg.desc: Socket WriteSocket (4E): source Write_Req, 80 bytes (the header and the whole Buf; BufLen says how many are sent)

Read_Msg.desc: Socket ReadSocket (4D): source Read_Req (8 bytes), destination Read_Resp

Inspect_Req.desc: The line asks for an inspection: write TRIG to Cam1 and read the answer. The level sets it and clears it

Write_Req.desc: WriteSocket's request: Timeout 5000 ms, BufLen and Buf from Trig_Cmd

Read_Resp.desc: ReadSocket's answer: BufLen bytes in Buf

Comma_Pos.desc: Where the comma is (1 is the first character; 0 none)

Verdict_Len.desc: How many characters the verdict has

Verdict.desc: The answer up to the comma

Score_Len.desc: How many characters the score has

Result_Pass.desc: The answer's verdict: 1 for PASS, 0 for FAIL

Insp_Done.desc: Set it when the result tags hold this inspection's answer; clear it when Inspect_Req drops
